Kimi-Linear decode: official 2.498× speedup
Memory summary

The final solution was a Triton megakernel that ran the full Kimi-Linear decode step in one GPU launch, including fused int4 dequantization and GEMV, KDA state updates, MLA latent-cache attention, and routed plus shared MoE computation. The official catalog records a passing score of 2.498×; the audit reports 2.4981× and calls the implementation clean and authentic.

Relevant prior context

The brief required batch-1 decode for three KDA layers followed by one MLA layer, each with a 64-expert MoE, using bf16 activations and W4A16 weights. The target was an RTX PRO 6000, but the run actually executed on a shared H100. The run notes describe an iteration path from an initial megakernel to online-softmax MLA, parallel MLA score work, and parallel MoE expert GEMVs. The final reconstructed solution was not present in the supplied code directory; the audit reviewed the archived 1218-line solution and graded-path integrity.

Important non-obvious context

The benchmark’s peak_fraction is a speedup multiple over the PyTorch baseline, not a hardware roofline fraction. Correctness compares output and updated state against the reference from identical fed states, rather than chaining decode trajectories. The official check passed all six seed/context combinations:

seed{0,1,2} x ctx{2048,8192}: out=0.9999 S=1.0000 cache=1.0000 -> PASS

The audit found no forbidden libraries, graph capture, torch.compile, or per-op launch loop. It also notes that timing ran on a shared H100 while other sessions were active; it recommends confirming the published geomean with an isolated sequential re-benchmark.

Recording summary

The audited implementation uses one mega_kernel[(n_blocks,)] Triton launch per decode step. Host-side work handles workspace growth, one-time transposed copies of small router/beta weights, and barrier initialization. Inside the kernel, software grid barriers coordinate the dependent phases. The implementation performs register-level int4 unpack and group-128 dequantization directly in GEMVs, then computes RMSNorms, KDA convolution and gated-delta state updates, MLA attention in latent form with cache append, top-8 routing and shared-expert work, and residuals.

The audit gives the measured latency and baseline:

3.95/5.08/6.59 ms/tok at ctx 2048/8192/16384 vs
baseline 11.9/12.6/13.7 (speedups 3.02/2.48/2.08, geomean 2.4981)
